title: Quantization Fidelity Gates - Architecture & KV Cache Sensitivity Sync
summary: Deep technical review of INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ tradeoffs observed in Argenta's on-prem pilot. Focus on where fidelity regressions were seen, KV cache and batching interactions, and proposed "gates" (fallback/precision gating) plus immediate test plan and config changes to mitigate.

Argenta to provide failing prompt set + top-3 model outputs by 2027-02-21
Schedule canary deployment with precision gate (int8->fp8 fallback) week of 2027-03-01
action_items: Priya Nair - run layerwise fidelity scan and upload results - 2027-02-24
Omar Haddad - export representative traffic trace and KV cache stats - 2027-02-21
Jordan Lee - share security whitepaper + KMS integration guide - 2027-02-22
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SRE), Lisa (Argenta Head ML), Omar (Argenta Platform), Rina (Argenta Security)
---
00:00 Jordan: okay cool uh thanks everyone for joining. I know we have a packed agenda, quick check on time, we have about 54 minutes, is that still good?
00:04 Lisa: yes that's fine, we—yeah we really wanna get to the regression triage.
00:08 Priya: great, agenda — quick recap of what we saw (int8's hit on a subset of prompts), then layerwise repro notes, kvcache interactions, batching/throughput tradeoffs, and then proposed "fidelity gates" for canary rollout.
00:15 Omar: quick note on infra — we're running on prem, nVidia H100s with MIG disabled, VPC peered for control plane, and strict egress, so anything that needs external endpoints will be vetted by Rina.
00:23 Jordan: got it. Rina, any high level constraints?
00:26 Rina: SOC2 controls need auditability for key material; we require KMS/HSM for key management. Also, no outbound telemetry containing raw PII — so any debugging traces must be redacted.
00:36 Priya: noted. OK starting with the observed failure mode — Lisa, can you restate the symptom?
00:40 Lisa: yeah so after switching our baseline to the AWQ-int8 profile the overall token cost dropped ~3x, throughput increased, latency improved slightly but the fraction of prompts where the summary was noticeably wrong rose from 0.4% to ~2.8%. Not catastrophic but with clinical notes that failure rate is not acceptable.
00:58 Jordan: and these are deterministic diffs? are they repeatable on the same seed / prompt?
01:03 Lisa: mostly yes, reproducible when we replay the same request and KV prefill. But when we warm the kvcache it seems to reduce some of the regressions — so there's an interaction.
01:13 Priya: ok that matches a hypothesis we've seen — quant noise amplifies on cold KV warmup and some tokens diverge, especially for longer context where kv cache is heavily used.
01:23 Marco: I want to call out one infra detail — your KV cache TTLs are set to 40s and you have very short-lived batch windows, so stale kv pointers happen more often. I think we need the traffic profile.
01:34 Omar: yes I can send the traces. We also have aggressive batching to get cost down — we batch up to 128 tokens per worker in production to saturate GPU utilization.
01:44 Priya: batching magnitude matters. AWQ/int8 paths sometimes change per-token probabilities, and with larger batches the KV state returns get interleaved differently; there can be subtle scheduling differences on the runtime that change the attention math micro-order.
01:58 Lisa: pause — can you explain micro-order? is that, like, nondeterministic?
02:02 Priya: not nondeterministic per se but a deterministic ordering difference in how the runtime processes multiple streams which can change floating rounding accumulation, and in quantized kernels that rounding error is larger, so the final tokens differ.
02:15 Jordan: so what are our levers? We have: 1) move to fp8 on sensitive layers, 2) enable per-layer GPTQ hybridization, 3) KV warmup cache priming, 4) precision-gating (detect prompts whose embedding distribution triggers fallback).
02:30 Lisa: what's the overhead of fp8 vs int8 for us? cost is key.
02:33 Priya: fp8 typically costs 10-20% more tokens on GPU time in our tests, but reduces fidelity regressions substantially for a subset of layers (attention/query/key/proj layers). Int8 has best perf/cost but is most prone to edge diffs.
02:45 Marco: and on our H100 fleet FP8 benefits from Tensor Cores but the kernel path is less optimized than the int8 AWQ kernels - so the perf delta varies per sequence length.
02:54 Omar: are there quick mitigations we can do while we run provenance tests?
02:58 Priya: yes — 1) gating via a cheap classifier on the prompt embeddings (if classifier says 'high risk' then route to fp8 path), 2) KV prefill/warmup heuristic where we keep short-term hot cache entries sticky for known prefixes, 3) reduce batch size for sensitive endpoints to minimize micro-order variance.
03:16 Lisa: classifier — can it be inference-only and small? we don't want extra infra.
03:20 Priya: yes, a small logistic or tiny transformer over embeddings, runs in CPU or a tiny GPU. Latency add is ~6-10ms, which for many of your summaries is acceptable.
03:29 Jordan: let's switch to the layerwise repro plan — Priya, what did you run?
03:32 Priya: I ran a layer perturbation sweep on a 1k prompt sample Argenta provided. For each layer we swapped quantized weights between int8 and fp16, and observed per-prompt logit divergence and token accuracy. We found 3 layers in mid-deep attention block that when kept in fp16/fp8 reduce regressions by ~75% while preserving 2.2x cost reduction overall.
03:52 Lisa: those layers sound promising. Can you give us the IDs?
03:55 Priya: I'll put the exact layer indices in the report but they map to blocks 14-16 in your 32-layer model, specifically Q/K projection and the final output projection of block 15.
04:06 Jordan: perfect. Any questions on the repro environment?
04:09 Omar: yes — is the repro run using the same KV cache state as production, or are you wiping it each time?
04:14 Priya: the sweep used a cold start (KV cleared) then we replayed the prefix to rebuild it. We also ran a warm-start sweep where we prefilled KV with top-k history and the diffs reduced — which supports the KV interaction hypothesis.
04:28 Marco: note that in our runtime we have optional sticky KV shards per worker; if you have high locality we can enable affinity, that reduces cross-worker KV hot misses. But it increases load skew.
04:39 Lisa: what's the tradeoff? we can't have hotspots.
04:42 Marco: we can enable soft affinity with a cap — keep a worker sticky for a user session for 5 minutes, then release, smoothing load but improving cache hit rate.
04:52 Rina: on security and telemetry — any change like sticky affinity or log collection has to be privacy-preserving. We need redaction and encryption at rest. Also any model weights movement off-prem is blocked.
05:03 Jordan: of course. Our private deploy model supports empty egress and on-prem weight residency; we can do the layerwise switches in your VPC so weights never leave.
05:12 Lisa: good. Can we talk about deterministic weirdness — seeds, FP nondet on different kernels? We saw slightly different outputs across restarts.
05:19 Priya: yes some kernels have nondeterminism due to CUDA atomics or different reduction orders. For strict determinism we can enable deterministic kernel flags but perf will drop. We typically recommend determinism only for eval runs not for full production.
05:32 Omar: what about hybrid mixing, like GPTQ for feedforward layers and AWQ for attention — is that supported?
05:38 Priya: yes we can do layerwise mixed quant. GPTQ tends to preserve accuracy better for dense feedforward while AWQ/int8 is fastest for matmuls, so a hybrid often gets the sweet spot. We already have a codepath in Redwood runtime to patch layers individually.
05:51 Lisa: do you have an example config?
05:54 Jordan: we'll share a sample config — it's essentially a per-layer map e.g. {layer: quant_backend}. We'll put a template in the report.
06:02 Priya: next, a short discussion on metrics — what metrics are must-haves for you to accept a rollout?
06:07 Lisa: accuracy on the 2k sentinel test set must not degrade more than 0.5% absolute, latency P95 must remain under 260ms, and cost per 1k tokens must be below our committed number.
06:19 Jordan: noted. We'll run canary with those gates. Canary logic: start with int8 with sticky kvcache + small batch, if sentinel fails run a fallback to fp8 for the failing percentiles.
06:29 Omar: what about tracing and redaction? we need to avoid PII in traces.
06:33 Marco: we can capture hashes and token positions instead of raw text; also we can store partial sketches for root cause without full PII — we'll document specifics.
06:44 Priya: a practical short-term plan — 1) run layerwise repro on the failing prompts, 2) run warm-start KV simulation to measure correction rate, 3) prototype embedding-based classifier for gating. Expected timeline two weeks.
06:55 Lisa: ok that's good. Also one more question on eval — how do you compare GPTQ vs AWQ on our dataset? we saw earlier that GPTQ sometimes had higher fidelity but was slower.
07:06 Priya: GPTQ is heavier to compile/quantize but runtime can be competitive; the accuracy delta tends to favor GPTQ in rare corner cases. Our recommendation: for critical endpoints choose GPTQ/fp8 for the sensitive layers and AWQ-int8 elsewhere. We have a tool to auto-propose layer mapping based on your eval metric.
07:24 Rina: any compliance concerns with GPTQ tooling? does it require external service?
07:28 Jordan: no, all tooling can run inside your VPC; for heavy compile we can deploy a sandboxed job runner on-prem that never leaves your network.
07:36 Omar: what about memory — fp8 increases model memory slightly; do we need bigger instances?
07:40 Marco: fp8 increases compute and memory footprint marginally, you might see a need to add ~8-12% extra buffer on large context runs. We'll include sizing guidance.
07:51 Lisa: let's review the concrete canary flow one more time.
07:54 Priya: 1) baseline int8 with sticky KV and reduced batch size for the canary, 2) run sentinel suite for 24 hours; if failure rate > 0.5% then dynamic fallback per-request to fp8 for that request and log for analysis, 3) after 72 hours, if sentinel stable, gradually increase batch size and relax sticky TTLs.
08:17 Jordan: Also add a layerwise hybrid preset as a second canary (apply the 3 identified layers in fp8).
08:22 Lisa: and who executes this?
08:24 Jordan: Redwood will run the layerwise repro and provide config, Argenta will run the canary in their VPC with Redwood remote ops assistance.
08:31 Omar: timeline recap?
08:33 Jordan: Priya's report by 02-24, Argenta traces by 02-21, security docs 02-22, canary starting week of 03-01.
08:42 Rina: we'll need an SOC2 addendum in the contract for on-prem operations, can you send that?
08:48 Jordan: yes I'll attach the addendum.
08:50 Lisa: couple more nitpicks — what about cold-start latencies for initial users? we saw double latency on cold with int8.
08:56 Priya: cold start penalty is due to KV warmup + kernel JIT compile path on first few inputs. We can pre-JIT and keep persistent warmed kernels in the worker; that adds some memory but reduces first-request latency.
09:10 Omar: is pre-JIT safe on our constrained nodes?
09:12 Marco: yes if you have reserved capacity we can reserve a warmed pool. In Dedicated mode Redwood has reserve pools. On-prem you can reserve a small pool too.
09:22 Lisa: ok. Anything else?
09:24 Jordan: I'll summarize and close. Action items and next steps as we listed: Priya will run layerwise fidelity scan and upload results (02-24), Omar to provide traces (02-21), Jordan to share security/KMS guide and SOC2 addendum (02-22). We'll schedule the canary for the week of 03-01. Any objections?
09:44 Lisa: none. Thanks everyone.
09:47 Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up in email with the report and config artifacts.
09:51 [call ends]
notes: Transcript contains some ASR artifacts: 'KV cash' occasionally, 'A-W-Q' for AWQ. Speakers sometimes truncated names. References: will attach layerwise-report.pdf, canary-config.yaml, security-addendum.pdf in follow-up email.
